title: Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2013
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2013 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) to increase, as of December 1, 2013, the rates of veterans' disability compensation, additional compensation for dependents, the clothing allowance for certain disabled veterans, and dependency and indemnity compensation for surviving spouses and children.

Requires each such increase to be the same percentage as the increase in benefits provided under title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) of the Social Security Act, on the same effective date.

summary.headline: This 2013 law raised VA disability compensation and related veterans' payments starting December 1, 2013, by the same percentage as the Social Security cost-of-living increase.
summary.what_it_does: The law directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to increase several monthly benefits as of December 1, 2013. These include disability compensation, extra payments for dependents, the clothing allowance for certain disabled veterans, and dependency and indemnity compensation for surviving spouses and children. Each increase matches the percentage raise in Social Security benefits under Title II of the Social Security Act, effective on the same date.

who_it_affects.how: Their monthly disability payments went up by the same percentage as the Social Security benefit increase.
The additional compensation paid for their spouses, children, or other dependents also increased by the same percentage.

who_it_affects.group: Certain disabled veterans eligible for the clothing allowance
who_it_affects.how: The yearly clothing allowance they receive was raised by the same percentage.

who_it_affects.group: Surviving spouses and children receiving dependency and indemnity compensation
who_it_affects.how: Their monthly survivor payments increased by the same percentage as the Social Security benefit increase.
